content: 1. There is no specific antiretroviral regimen that is universally preferred for individuals living with HIV. 2. Nandi Siegfried disclosed that she has provided consultation services to the World Health Organization (WHO). 3. Ezio Távora dos Santos Filho reported delivering a presentation at the Regional International AIDS Society conference in April 2018 in Mexico City. His talk focused on the need for advanced tools for tuberculosis (TB) infection treatment, but he did not endorse any specific study. He also stated that, as a TB advocate, he has participated in numerous discussions with the Global TB Community Advisory Board and the Brazilian National TB Community Advisory Board (CAB) regarding the implementation of new TB infection treatment methods. 4. The Brazilian TB CAB is currently raising awareness about the 3HP regimen and TB infection. Communities affected by TB may directly benefit from the introduction of new guidelines. 5. Marieke van der Werf disclosed that her employer, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control, has an interest in TB infection and is actively working on related issues. 6. Wim Vandevelde reported receiving travel support from the Stop TB Partnership to participate as a speaker in the TB/HIV symposium at the International AIDS Society conference in 2019 in Mexico City. The symposium addressed TB infection. 7. Members of the External Review Group (ERG) who declared no conflicts of interest with the objectives of the guidelines include Stephen Graham, Giovanni B. Migliori, Rohit Sarin, and Alena Skrahina. 8. ERG members who declared interests that were deemed not to conflict with WHO policies or the meeting objectives include: Connie Erkens, who disclosed involvement in a study on TB infection screening in migrants to the Netherlands. The study received 1,800 Quantiferon-TB Gold Plus tests from QIAGEN (valued at EUR 27,000) between 2016 and 2018. QIAGEN had no role in the study design, implementation, data collection, analysis, or publication decisions. James Seddon, who is employed by Imperial College London to conduct research on childhood TB. He holds a grant from the Global Trials Scheme to conduct a trial on preventive therapy for children and adolescents exposed to multidrug-resistant TB (MDR-TB). He also has a fellowship from the Medical Research Council to study risk correlates in MDR-TB-exposed children and adolescents. He is involved in the TB-CHAMP trial, which focuses on MDR-TB prevention in children under five years old, and collaborates on modeling exercises funded by the TB Modelling and Analysis Consortium (TB-MAC) to evaluate TB infection treatment strategies. He has also written reviews on TB infection and treatment. Carrie Tudor, who is employed by the International Council of Nurses, which received US $1 million from the Eli Lilly Foundation MDR-TB partnership to train nurses between 2013 and 2019. 9. Evidence reviewers provided estimates for evidence summaries but did not participate in formulating policy recommendations. 10. Lynn M. Mofenson disclosed that she served as a consultant for WHO in 2018 on the use of dolutegravir during pregnancy. 11. Members of the Expert Group were selected to represent diverse perspectives, including technical experts, end-users, patient representatives, and evidence synthesis methodologists. Participation in discussions and follow-up dialogue was limited to those who attended the Expert Group meeting in person. 12. Expert Group members were required to submit completed declarations of interest (DOI) forms, which were reviewed by the WHO legal department before the meeting. DOI statements were summarized by the co-chair of the meeting, Karin Weyer, at the start of the session. 13. WHO consolidated guidelines on tuberculosis include recommendations for tests to diagnose TB infection. 14. P. Hill and R. O’Brien disclosed minor conflicts of interest. P. Hill received kits from Cellestis (now QIAGEN) and Oxford Immunotec for research projects. R. O’Brien received support from the Foundation for Innovative New Diagnostics (FIND) for academic collaborations on developing a point-of-care serodiagnostic test and biomarker discovery projects. 15. Selected individuals with intellectual or research involvement in the use of interferon-gamma release assays (IGRAs) in lowand middle-income settings were invited as observers to provide technical input and answer questions. These individuals did not participate in the GRADE evaluation process, meeting discussions, or the development of the final WHO policy statement. 16. P. Godfrey-Faussett disclosed a research grant for investigating the use of the Quantiferon-TB Gold In-Tube assay in South Africa and Zambia. M. Pai disclosed conducting research studies on IGRAs. 17. Systematic reviewers (A. Cattamanchi, A. Date, A. Detjen, D. Dowdy, R. Menzies, J. Metcalfe, M. Pai, M. Rangaka, K. Steingart, and A. Zwerling) were deemed to have conflicts of interest and participated as observers, providing technical clarifications on systematic review findings. They did not participate in the GRADE evaluation process, meeting discussions, or the development of the final WHO policy statement.
